newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts welcome Philips axe on Superclub.
newsitem.headline: Analysts welcome Philips axe on Superclub.

text.p: Analysts welcomed Philips NV's decision on Wednesday to wind up its loss-making Superclub video-rental subsidiary.
Philips earlier said it would wind up Superclub on April 1 due to losses which made further operations "irresponsible".

Superclub, with operations in Belgium and The Netherlands, is a chain of shops selling and renting videotapes and selling audio CDs, computer games and multi-media entertainment packages such as CD-interactive and CD-Rom.
"Philips should have done this eight years ago," said Agatho van Hilst of broker Amstgeld.
Rene Verhoef of NIBStrating estimated that Superclub could have lost Philips up to 20 million guilders last year.
Analysts said closing down Superclub fitted Philips chairman Cor Boonstra's strategy for the group's future.
"Back to the core business," said Van Hilst.
Another analyst said it was clear that more plant and Philips' units would be closed.
"Sound & Vision isn't doing that well," said Edwin Flick of Rabo Effecten. "Lighting margins are also under pressure."
"It's not yet clear what will happen, but there's more to come," Flick added.
Last week Philips announced it planned to loosen its ties with loss-making German associate Grundig.
